title: Test: fit one Survey Scanner I at Central Nexus, so that one scout can survey_system (hidden places, deep core deposits, the scanning skill)
note: Kept by Oracle; written 2026-11-17 07:21 UTC (orders.log ENT-029, task 1 and block ORACLE). The catalog (table skills) says scanning rises on querying a place or surveying a system and deep core mining on revealing deep core deposits with survey_system; exploration adds survey power. Every scout stands at scanning 0 (table ship_skills, 2026-11-17 07:20 UTC): the census reads get_poi and has never surveyed. survey_system needs a survey scanner (Survey Scanner I: utility slot, cpu 3, power 4, survey power 30, catalog 0.723.2; a Threshold has 2 utility slots, cpu 16, power 30, and a scout fits a mining laser in one). Since 0.722.0 the game asks frontier explorers to survey again. The question the test answers: does a survey show places or ores (uranium, seam glass, silicon) the census does not. Central Nexus asked 4,892 cr for 1 and The Experiment 4,911 for 2 (books of 07:14 and 07:18 UTC); max_price 5,000 with the 1 percent tax. One scout; the first survey_system is flown by hand (rule F29), then a survey step for the census is built if it shows more than get_poi. Changed by Oracle 2026-11-17 19:26 UTC: max_pilots 2 -> 7, for five readers. The test answered: 12 surveys beyond the border (scouting/<system>.json `survey`, 15:37 to 19:15 UTC) revealed no hidden deposit; at Homam and The Telescope the game answered "Survey detected 1 faint signature(s) that your scanner cannot resolve. Try a more powerful survey scanner." The scanner scout stands at scanning 1, every other scout at 0 (table ship_skills, 19:20 UTC): a survey is the one census action that trains the class's scanning skill. Five readers fly the most frequent lists (the outpost watch every 35 minutes), so their next rows say whether a survey of a system surveyed before still pays scanning XP.
